name: M5Launcher
label: M5Launcher (bmorcelli) — multi-board firmware launcher
description: bmorcelli's Launcher (formerly M5Stick-Launcher) — a multi-board boot menu that loads other firmwares (Marauder, Bruce, and any .bin) from an SD card, plus an over-the-air app store. One codebase, ~70 board targets from bare ESP32 through the M5Stack Cardputer/CoreS3/StickC family, the Cheap Yellow Display fleet, and many LilyGo boards. Per-board merged single .bin flashed at 0x0. The launcher itself transmits nothing; any offensive capability belongs to the firmware you subsequently load, which carries its own profile + danger label.
note: bmorcelli/Launcher (aka M5Launcher; the repo was renamed from M5Stick-Launcher). Live-verified via gh 2026-08-31: latest tag v2.8.0 ships 70 per-board Launcher-<board>.bin assets. Each is a MERGED single image flashed at 0x0 — confirmed by inspecting Launcher-m5stack-cardputer.bin (0xE9 image magic at 0x0, partition-table magic 0xAA50 at 0x8000). github_release resolver tracks the latest release and emits every matched asset as a board variant; chip family is derived from the filename fragments (default esp32, with s3/c5/c6 rules), and esptool auto-detects the real chip at flash time, so the merged-at-0x0 write is offset-correct on every board. No per-asset SHA pin (rolling latest, same model as bruce.json). danger="": Launcher is a boot menu / app loader that authors no TX; the offensive capability lives in whatever firmware you load onto it, which brings its own profile + danger label. protocol=null (a boot menu has no persistent serial control grammar). Chip labels for a handful of newer boards (e.g. m5stack-tab5 = ESP32-P4, some large CYDs) fall back to the esp32 default and are cosmetic under merged-at-0x0 auto-detect; real-hardware flash owner-gated (Phase-F).
